summary: Fork Mountain, Madison County, VA: state fire tower built 1929 about a mile from President Hoover's camp; taken down by 1954, with footings noted in 1957.

facts.design: 35-foot steel tower with an inside stairway, per 1929 newspapers; the observation cab was planned at about 6 by 8 feet
facts.status_note: Taken down by 1954; a 1957 survey still noted the concrete footings.

events.note: One of three steel towers the state forest service built in 1929 (1929 newspaper quotes)
Watchman Douglas Seal named at the site; the page describes a metal tower of another model
Army Corps of Engineers check found the tower removed, concrete footings left
Coast and Geodetic Survey log calls the summit Fort Mountain and notes the lookout's cement foundations remain

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1929 newspapers and the Forest Fire Lookout Association say Fork Mountain; the 1957 survey log says Fort Mountain. The story uses Fork.
1929 newspapers describe a 35-foot tower; the 1940 page describes a metal tower of another model and says both towers look similar in height, so the sources do not settle which tower stood in 1940.

notes_for_editor: Built year, design and the 1954 removal rest on 1929 newspaper quotes and a volunteer history page (WillhiteWeb) that cites USGS survey notes; the originals were not checked. The 1940 tower is described differently from the 1929 one (see resolved_conflicts). No source read describes the summit today; the 1957 footings note is the latest. The record's coordinates were not checked against a survey point.
